He was deeply immersed in the local community and student networks of Santiago, which gave him direct domain exposure to the anti-Batista movement. He built a clandestine cell-based revolutionary organization from 1953 at age 19, merging with Castro's movement in 1955 and leading the November 30, 1956 armed uprising in Santiago at age 21. The adversity of poverty and dictatorship catalyzed his revolutionary commitment.

name: Esma Redžepova
milestone_by_age_26: Won a school talent contest for Radio Skopje in 1956 at age 13, performing the first Romani-language song ever aired on the station, beating 57 other schools; this launched her professional career under manager Stevo Teodosievski.
early_history_summary: Born in Skopje to a poor Xoraxane Muslim Roma family, Redžepova was introduced to Romani music at age 9 by her brother. In 1956, her headteacher entered her in a Radio Skopje talent contest, which she won with a Romani traditional song — the first Romani-language song broadcast on the station. This brought her to the attention of Stevo Teodosievski, who became her mentor, manager, and later husband.
family_context_summary: Born into a poor Xoraxane Muslim Roma family in Skopje. Father Ibrahim lost a leg in a German bombing and worked as a porter, circus strongman, and shoeshiner. Mother was a seamstress. Family had traditional expectations that Esma would marry in her teens.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father sang and played drums at weddings; some siblings accompanied him. Brother introduced Esma to a local Romani music organization at age 9. Musical environment in the family but not professional training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stevo Teodosievski mentorship, Radio Skopje platform, Romani musical heritage, poverty-driven urgency
evidence_summary: Redžepova was born into deep poverty in Skopje's Romani community, with a disabled father and seamstress mother. Her brother introduced her to Romani music at age 9, and her father's informal musical performances at weddings provided early exposure. At 13, she won a Radio Skopje talent contest singing the first Romani-language song aired on the station, which brought her to the attention of Stevo Teodosievski, who became her dedicated mentor and manager. Teodosievski trained her intensively, enrolled her at the Academy of Music in Belgrade, and built her career through the Ansambl Teodosievski. The adversity of Romani poverty and cultural barriers against female performers catalyzed her determination.
starting_point: Born into a poor Xoraxane Muslim Roma family in Skopje; father was a disabled shoeshiner who lost a leg in wartime bombing, mother was a seamstress.
current_position: Died on December 11, 2016 at age 73 in Skopje, Macedonia; final status: internationally renowned Romani singer known as 'Queen of the Gypsies,' NPR 50 Great Voices, over 580 recorded songs and 22,000 concerts.

trajectory.event: Won a school talent contest for Radio Skopje, performing the first Romani-language song aired on the station, beating 57 other schools.

Died on December 11, 2016 in Skopje after a short illness.
